reach: Both problems are library-only: production does not reach engcore.hybrid_uq. Inside it, both rules land on the SUPPLIED-grid route (router.py step 1), the REBUILT-grid route (router.py step 3 via _rebuild_grid) and routed prediction (predictive.py's grid chain) -- the three callers of the V2 grid-evidence checks. The V1 resolution check in src/engcore/inference/calibration.py is NOT touched: I-05's own title says 'additive checks, V1 digest unmoved', so the new checks live in the V2 layer and import V1's declared constants and its exact aliasing enumeration rather than changing them.

what_was_already_seen.R-05: _fitted_lattice_covariance fits ONE least-squares quadratic about the global argmax, over a window of 50 nats or more, with no test of how well it fits, and floors flat or convex directions to 'cannot alias'. _grid_resolution_refusal never looks at any other local maximum. The verifier's correction to the mechanism matters: the check does not pass because the step resolves the broad mode -- the 50-nat window pools nodes from BOTH modes, so the fitted quadratic is polluted, its lattice variance comes out at 285 to 7e3 or at the 1e12 floor, and the aliasing number reaches 1.5e4 to 4e13. The second mode switches the aliasing check OFF. On the audited case (a(t) = t^2 for t >= 0 and (8t)^2 below; modes at +0.99 with local sd 0.00519 and at -0.124 with local sd 0.00065) a step of 0.005 gives GRID_AS_SUPPLIED SUPPORTED PARAMETERS_IDENTIFIABLE with narrow-mode mass 0.0005 against a true 0.1111, a mean error of +0.35 sd and an sd ratio of 0.070. A scan of 20 grid offsets gave SUPPORTED on all 20. The smooth model e^t + e^-8t does it too, so it is not the kink. On the rebuild path K = 9 gives SUPPORTED with narrow-mode mass 0.209 against 0.100 and a mean error of -0.36 sd.
what_was_already_seen.R-17: grid_containment takes each face's peak over ADMISSIBLE nodes only, so a face with no admissible node scores -inf and passes. A posterior cut off inside the box by the forward evaluator's refusal therefore never reaches a face. The router refuses a supplied grid whose posterior reaches a DECLARED-BOUND face and halves steps at such a face in a rebuild; the same hard cut made by admissibility gets neither. On the audited case (the forward model refuses t0 < 1.0, the unconstrained optimum at the cut, step 0.9 sd) cut offsets of 0.02, 0.50 and 0.98 steps give GRID_AS_SUPPLIED SUPPORTED PARAMETERS_IDENTIFIABLE with mean errors of -0.40, +0.05 and +0.57 true sd and sd ratios 1.092, 0.933 and 0.787 against a 4001-node reference that matches truncated-normal theory. The control with the box face at the same place is REFUSED GRID_DOES_NOT_CONTAIN_POSTERIOR. The rebuild ends SUPPORTED with '0 truncation halving(s)' and a mean error of -0.144 sd, about 3x the router's own TRUNCATION_CONVERGENCE_SD of 0.05.

every_local_maximum_in_the_band_is_a_mod.rule: A mode is an INTERIOR node of the tensor lattice, admissible and with a finite log-likelihood, within EDGE_LOG_LIKELIHOOD_DROP = ln 1e6 of the peak, whose log-likelihood is at least that of every one of its 3^p - 1 lattice neighbours. The global argmax is always one. Each is checked on its own; a grid with any unchecked or failing mode is passed over with the new reason GRID_MODE_UNRESOLVED.
every_local_maximum_in_the_band_is_a_mod.why_the_full_stencil: over the 2p AXIS neighbours alone, an exactly Gaussian tilted ridge produces a staircase of spurious maxima: measured on hybrid_synthetic.affine at 41 and 61 nodes per axis, 3 and 4 of them. Over the full 3^p - 1 stencil the same grids have exactly ONE maximum.
every_local_maximum_in_the_band_is_a_mod.why_spurious_maxima_are_harmless: a thin tilted ridge can still staircase over the full stencil when its crest passes between nodes: measured on hybrid_synthetic.bimodal_two_parameter at 41 nodes per axis, 11 maxima, on a grid whose moments are stable to 6 digits from 41 to 321 nodes per axis. Each of those 11 yields the RIDGE's own curvature, so each passes both tests below with a wide margin (worst fit residual 0.50 nats against a bound of 4.61, and every aliasing number above the V1 minimum). So the rule does not need mode-finding to be exact -- it needs it to MISS nothing, which is why maximality is non-strict and the band is the one the containment check already uses.
every_local_maximum_in_the_band_is_a_mod.class: A (a definition over an already-declared band, with no new constant)

each_mode_gets_its_own_curvature_fit.rule: About each mode, a least-squares quadratic in LATTICE units (node coordinates minus the mode's, divided by _tensor_lattice_steps, which is V1's own convention) over the smallest lattice box radius whose usable nodes number at least 2 * ((p + 1)(p + 2) / 2) -- the same node count V1's resolution check already requires. Flat and convex directions are floored exactly as V1 floors them (_FLAT_DIRECTION_PRECISION, _FLAT_DIRECTION_RELATIVE_PRECISION). A mode about which no such fit exists (too few usable nodes, a singular design) is UNRESOLVED.
each_mode_gets_its_own_curvature_fit.why: the audited defect is a single fit over a 50-nat window pooling two modes. A box of a few lattice steps about one maximum cannot pool another mode's nodes, which is what makes the fitted curvature that mode's own. Measured: on the audited case at step 0.008 the narrow mode's own fit gives a lattice sd of 0.109 steps and an aliasing number of 0.470, against the pooled fit's 285 to 7e3.
each_mode_gets_its_own_curvature_fit.class: A (V1's node count, V1's lattice units, V1's floors; the only new thing is the LOCALITY)

a_fit_that_does_not_describe_its_own_nod.rule: The fit is adequate only when its largest absolute residual over the fitted nodes is at most MODE_FIT_RESIDUAL_NATS. A mode whose fit is not adequate is UNRESOLVED.
a_fit_that_does_not_describe_its_own_nod.why: the aliasing bound is declared as an amplitude: _ALIASING_NUMBER_MINIMUM = 2 ln 100 is the value at which the aliased component's amplitude exp(-A / 2) is 1 %. Expressed in the log-density the check works in, that tolerance IS ln 100 nats. So the rule is: a fitted quadratic may not deviate from the log-likelihoods it was fitted to by more than the log-amplitude the aliasing criterion itself tolerates. Nothing is tuned: the number is the existing constant halved, and it is the same statement the existing constant makes.
a_fit_that_does_not_describe_its_own_nod.measured_margins: worst fit residual: affine 0.0 nats, bimodal_two_parameter's 11-maximum staircase 0.50, the audited case at a step of 0.0005 (resolved) 0.0043 -- all far below 4.61; the audited case's narrow mode at step 0.008 is 17.7 and hybrid_synthetic.mirror_mode on a 61-node grid is 8.7, both far above. The measured separation is a factor of 9 on the passing side and a factor of 1.9 on the failing side.
a_fit_that_does_not_describe_its_own_nod.class: B (a restatement of the already-preregistered aliasing amplitude in the units the fit is measured in)

each_mode_is_held_to_v1s_own_aliasing_bo.rule: A mode's fitted lattice covariance is passed to V1's own exact enumeration, _minimum_aliasing_number(cov, _ALIASING_NUMBER_MINIMUM). A mode for which it returns a number -- an off-axis lattice direction along which the mode is narrower than the grid can sample -- is UNRESOLVED.
each_mode_is_held_to_v1s_own_aliasing_bo.why: this is the check V1 already declares and validates; the audited defect is not the bound, it is that the bound was evaluated once, on a polluted fit. Re-deriving a new bound would replace a validated constant with an unvalidated one.
each_mode_is_held_to_v1s_own_aliasing_bo.class: A (V1's constant and V1's enumeration, unchanged)

an_admissibility_cut_is_a_truncation_fac.rule: An admissible node with a finite log-likelihood within EDGE_LOG_LIKELIHOOD_DROP of the peak that has an INADMISSIBLE or non-finite AXIS neighbour inside the lattice is a truncation face on that axis. On a supplied grid the grid is passed over with the new reason GRID_CUT_BY_INADMISSIBILITY, exactly as a declared-bound face is passed over today. In a rebuild that axis joins the truncation halving, so steps across the cut are halved until the moments move less than TRUNCATION_CONVERGENCE_SD.
an_admissibility_cut_is_a_truncation_fac.why: the router already holds that truncated moments cannot be shown to have converged without refinement, and acts on it at declared bounds. A cut made by the forward model's admissible region is the same hard edge: the V1 aliasing argument assumes a smooth density and does not bound the O(step) error at a cut. The audited case shows the error is real and one-sided, up to +0.57 true sd in the mean with the sd 0.79 of the truth.
an_admissibility_cut_is_a_truncation_fac.why_not_the_existing_reason: GRID_DOES_NOT_CONTAIN_POSTERIOR says the box is too small -- grow it. This says the ADMISSIBLE REGION ends inside the box, which growing cannot fix and refinement can. A reader who cannot tell the two apart cannot act on either.
an_admissibility_cut_is_a_truncation_fac.the_cut_is_not_the_bound: an axis cut by admissibility on both sides is NOT reported as GRID_POSTERIOR_BOUND_DOMINATED: that reason is about the DECLARED range being what the width describes, and an admissibility cut is the model's own domain. The rebuild keeps the two lists separate and runs the bound-domination check before the cuts are added to the halving list.
an_admissibility_cut_is_a_truncation_fac.class: A (an existing rule applied to a face the existing rule did not see, with no new constant)

both_checks_run_wherever_a_grid_is_held_.rule: grid_mode_resolution and grid_admissibility_truncation join grid_prior_uniformity, grid_goodness_of_fit and grid_containment in all three chains: the router's supplied-grid route, _grid_evidence.supplied_grid_problem, and predictive.py's routed prediction. A rebuilt grid runs the mode check after V1's resolution check and, when a mode is unresolved, the existing refinement retry runs again at four times the aliasing target rather than the grid being used.
both_checks_run_wherever_a_grid_is_held_.why: R-05's own reproduction reaches both the supplied and the rebuilt route, and the audit's improvement says to re-apply the checks in routed prediction.

a_grid_with_more_maxima_than_can_be_chec.rule: When the number of modes in the band exceeds MODE_FIT_LIMIT the grid is passed over with GRID_MODE_UNRESOLVED rather than each mode being fitted.
a_grid_with_more_maxima_than_can_be_chec.why: the check must terminate on a grid of any size, and a node log-likelihood with more than a thousand local maxima within a factor 1e6 of its peak is not a resolved sampling of a smooth posterior -- it is noise or aliasing, which is what the reason says. The measured counts on real grids are 1, 2 and 11, so the limit is two orders of magnitude above anything a resolved grid produces. It bounds the work at 1024 small least-squares fits.
a_grid_with_more_maxima_than_can_be_chec.class: C (a work limit, with the measured counts three orders of magnitude below it)

compatibility_impact.v1_frozen_symbols: untouched. src/engcore/inference/calibration.py is not edited: the new checks IMPORT _tensor_lattice_steps, _minimum_aliasing_number, _ALIASING_NUMBER_MINIMUM, _FLAT_DIRECTION_PRECISION and _FLAT_DIRECTION_RELATIVE_PRECISION from it and add a V2 layer above it.
v2_symbols: RouteReason: two members APPENDED after the last existing one -- GRID_MODE_UNRESOLVED and GRID_CUT_BY_INADMISSIBILITY, both refusals. No member is removed, renamed or reordered.
_grid_evidence gains two module-level functions and one keyword argument with a default on supplied_grid_problem; the module is private.
router._rebuild_grid gains no argument: the admissibility cuts join the truncation list it already keeps.
compatibility_impact.serialized_records: NOTHING changes. Both checks are router-side verdicts on a grid object, like the containment and uniformity checks beside them; no record field is added and no schema is bumped. A grid record already written is unaffected on read, because these checks run where a grid is ADMITTED, not where a record is parsed.
claims_that_move: a supplied grid with an unresolved mode in the ln 1e6 band is passed over (was: GRID_AS_SUPPLIED SUPPORTED) -- R-05's case;
a supplied grid cut inside its box by the forward model's admissible region is passed over (was: GRID_AS_SUPPLIED SUPPORTED) -- R-17's case;
a rebuilt grid with an unresolved mode is refined and, if it stays unresolved, passed over (was: used);
a rebuilt grid cut by admissibility has that axis halved until its moments converge (was: '0 truncation halving(s)');
routed prediction from such a grid raises instead of returning, as it already does for a misfit or an uncontained posterior.
compatibility_impact.committed_evidence: TCR.json's two grids are the cheap records most likely to move: both are +/- 6 OLS standard errors wide and are asserted to be used. Every committed grid claim is re-derived by running the new checks against the grids their generators build, and the audit document records the outcome. KINETICS_K2.json's reference grids and BATTERY_T41.json are SUPERSEDED and must not be re-run; their markers gain an entry stating what the rules say about the grids their bytes describe.

residuals_stated_in_advance: Mode finding is a property of the NODES, not of the posterior: a mode that falls entirely between nodes is not a local maximum of the node function and is not checked. That is the aliasing the V1 bound exists to catch at the maxima that ARE visible, and it is why the rule is a necessary and not a sufficient condition for resolution.

A mode on a FACE of the lattice is not interior and is not checked as a mode. It is already the containment check's business: density on a face within ln 1e6 of the peak passes a supplied grid over today.

The per-mode fit inherits the quadratic assumption. A mode whose log-likelihood is badly non-quadratic over a few lattice steps fails the residual test and is called unresolved, which is the safe direction but can be a false refusal for a genuinely resolved, genuinely non-Gaussian mode. The margin measured on real grids is a factor of 9.

The work is O(N * 3^p) for the scan plus one small least-squares fit per mode. For the tensor grids this route builds (exponential in p, so small p) that is cheap, but it is not free, and MODE_FIT_LIMIT is the declared bound on the fitting half.

An admissibility cut that is not axis-aligned is only partly seen: the rule looks along lattice axes, so a diagonal cut is detected wherever it separates axis neighbours, which it does, but the halving that follows refines only the axes where a neighbour pair straddles it. The verifier measured that a diagonal cut mostly averages the moment error out (< 0.02 sd), so the case that matters is the axis-aligned one.

The rebuild halves steps across a cut until the moments converge; it does not move the box to the cut. A posterior whose mass sits right against an admissibility boundary therefore still costs refinement rather than being reparameterized, and the O(step) error at the cut is bounded by TRUNCATION_CONVERGENCE_SD rather than removed.
amendments: recorded here as dated entries, never edited in place

amendment_log.change: `_grid_modes` returns the lattice AXES with the lattice and the modes, and `_mode_lattice_covariance` takes them.
amendment_log.why: the preregistered rule says the fit is in lattice units -- 'node coordinates minus the mode's, divided by _tensor_lattice_steps', which is V1's convention. For a UNIFORM axis that equals the index offset; for a non-uniform axis it does not, because _tensor_lattice_steps returns the axis's LARGEST step. Index offsets would have silently been a different quantity on a non-uniform axis, so the axes are carried and the coordinates are used.
amendment_log.why_this_is_not_a_threshold_change: no threshold; it is the rule as preregistered rather than an approximation to it.

amendment_log.change: The global argmax is a mode exactly when it is INTERIOR, not unconditionally.
amendment_log.why: the preregistered rule says both 'A mode is an INTERIOR node' and 'The global argmax is always one'. The argmax always satisfies the maximality half (maximality is non-strict), so the two only differ when the argmax sits on a FACE of the lattice -- and that case is already the containment check's, which passes a supplied grid over when density reaches a face. The stated residual says so: 'A mode on a FACE of the lattice is not interior and is not checked as a mode.' Interiority governs, and no special case for the argmax exists.
amendment_log.why_this_is_not_a_threshold_change: no threshold; it resolves which of two sentences in the rule is load-bearing, in the direction the residual already stated.

amendment_log.stage: after the first guard-mutation run, before the batch was committed
amendment_log.change: Two of sixteen mutations SURVIVED the first run, and two tests were added.
detail: removing the RESIDUAL test survived, because the audited case is caught by the aliasing bound too. Added test_r05_a_mode_the_aliasing_bound_passes_can_still_fail_its_own_fit: a broad shoulder with a narrow spike at its centre, where the least-squares quadratic follows the six shoulder nodes so its curvature is wide and V1's bound PASSES, while the centre node sits 6.67 nats below the fit (the bound is 4.61).

removing the ALIASING bound survived, because the audited case is caught by the residual test too. Added test_r05_a_mode_its_own_fit_describes_perfectly_can_still_fail_the_aliasing_bound: hybrid_synthetic's thin tilted ridge, whose log-likelihood is exactly quadratic (residual 1e-10 nats) and whose perpendicular width is below the lattice step.
so the two halves of the per-mode check are now each measured by a case the other half does not cover, which is what a surviving mutation is supposed to buy.
amendment_log.why_this_is_not_a_threshold_change: no threshold, class or value in `rules` is touched.

amendment_log.change: One mutation is recorded as an EXPECTED survivor: adding the admissibility cut axes to the list the bound-domination rule counts.
amendment_log.why: the guard against reporting the model's own domain as the declared range dominating a width is the ORDER of two statements -- the domination check reads the truncation list above the line where the cuts are merged into it. A mutation that appends the cuts after that line changes nothing, and the mutation that moves the domination check's own expression to read them (B12o) is KILLED. The ordering is the guard, and it is the ordering that is mutated.

amendment_log.change: No committed evidence was regenerated: nothing moved.
amendment_log.why: TCR.json's two supplied grids are the cheap records these rules could move, and they are re-derived live by tests/hybrid_uq/test_hybrid_uq_tcr.py::test_the_local_route_agrees_with_the_resolved_grid, which asserts GRID_AS_SUPPLIED and still passes -- so both grids resolve every mode in their band and neither is cut by admissibility. PERFORMANCE.json's V1 grid measurements are V1-only and unaffected. KINETICS_K2.json and BATTERY_T41.json are SUPERSEDED and were not re-run; their markers gain an entry.
